---
title: "Introduction to Git and GitHub"
---

A beginner-friendly training on version control with Git and GitHub, written for NV OSE staff and public health professionals. No prior experience needed.

## Overview

- **Audience:** Anyone new to Git and GitHub: epidemiologists, analysts, and program staff
- **Level:** Beginner
- **Duration:** About 3 hours (can be split into two sessions)
- **Format:** Workshop or self-paced

## Learning objectives

By the end of this training, you will be able to:

1. Explain the difference between **Git** and **GitHub**, and why version control matters.
2. Create a repository with a **README** and a **.gitignore**.
3. Make, commit, push, and pull changes using **GitHub Desktop** and the **command line**.
4. Use **branches** and **pull requests** to collaborate safely, and explain what a **fork** is.
5. Choose between **public and private** repositories.
6. Keep **data, passwords, and API tokens** out of GitHub, and know what to do if something is committed by mistake.

## Prerequisites

- A free [GitHub account](https://github.com/signup) with two-factor authentication turned on
- [GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com/) installed
- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads) installed (for the command-line lesson)
- A text editor, such as [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) or RStudio

::: {.callout-note}
On a state computer you may need IT to install software. Request it ahead of time.
:::
